items.definition: Expecting good things to happen.
items.example: He is optimistic that the team will finish on time.

items.definition: Expecting that something bad or unfavorable will happen.
items.example: She was pessimistic about her chances of winning.

items.definition: So good or so large that it is surprising.
items.example: The response to the new course has been phenomenal.

items.definition: Not willing to do something, and therefore slow to do it.
items.example: He was reluctant to share his notes before the exam.

items.definition: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
items.example: With so many delays, a later launch date was inevitable.

items.definition: Doubting that something is true or that it will work.
items.example: Investors remain skeptical about the company's forecast.

items.definition: Able to be understood in more than one way, so the meaning is unclear.
items.example: The instructions were ambiguous, so half the class did the wrong task.

items.definition: Strong enough to convince you, or interesting enough to hold your attention.
items.example: She made a compelling case for changing the schedule.

items.definition: Able to recover quickly after something difficult happens.
items.example: Small businesses here proved surprisingly resilient after the flood.

items.definition: Saying what is needed in few words.
items.example: Keep the summary concise so people actually read it.

items.definition: Done suddenly because you want to, without planning it.
items.example: We took a spontaneous trip to the coast on Saturday.

items.definition: Reasonable enough to be believed, even if it is not proven.
items.example: That is a plausible explanation, but we should still check the data.

items.definition: Very careful about small details.
items.example: He keeps meticulous records of every experiment.

items.definition: Large enough to matter.
items.example: There was a substantial drop in costs after the change.

items.definition: So small or unimportant that it is not worth worrying about.
items.example: We spent an hour arguing about a trivial detail.

items.definition: Clear and logically connected, so it is easy to follow.
items.example: Your essay needs a coherent argument, not just a list of facts.

items.definition: Continuing to try, or continuing to happen, over a long time.
items.example: Her persistent questions finally got us a straight answer.

items.definition: Possible to do with the time, money, or tools you have.
items.example: Finishing by Friday is feasible if two more people help.

items.definition: No longer used because something newer has replaced it.
items.example: The old file format became obsolete within a few years.

items.definition: Able to be trusted to do what is expected.
items.example: We need a reliable way to back up the files.

items.definition: Complete, leaving out nothing important.
items.example: The report was thorough and answered every question we had.

items.definition: Saying what you think very directly, even if it sounds rude.
items.example: To be blunt, the design is not ready to ship.

items.definition: Not needed because the same thing already exists somewhere else.
items.example: The last paragraph is redundant; it repeats the introduction.

items.definition: Useful in many different situations, or able to do many things well.
items.example: A good notebook app is versatile enough for work and study.

items.definition: Boring because it is slow and repetitive.
items.example: Checking each row by hand is tedious but necessary.

items.definition: To accept or admit that something is true, or to show that you received something.
items.example: She acknowledged the mistake and explained how she would fix it.

items.definition: To give special importance or attention to something.
items.example: The teacher emphasized that the deadline would not move.

items.definition: To expect something and get ready for it.
items.example: We anticipate a busy week, so plan your time carefully.

items.definition: To make something easier to understand.
items.example: Could you clarify what you mean by "soon"?

items.definition: To move something to a later time.
items.example: They postponed the meeting until Thursday morning.

items.definition: To officially give a share of money, time, or space to something.
items.example: We allocated two hours a day to language practice.

items.definition: To make something bad less severe.
items.example: Regular backups mitigate the damage when a drive fails.

items.definition: To gradually weaken something, often without it being obvious.
items.example: Missing small deadlines undermines trust over time.

items.definition: To make room for someone or something, or to change plans to help someone.
items.example: The schedule can accommodate one more presenter.

items.definition: To pause before doing something because you are unsure.
items.example: Don't hesitate to ask if the task is unclear.

items.definition: To give a good reason for something you did or want to do.
items.example: It is hard to justify the extra cost with these numbers.

items.definition: To make a process simpler and more efficient by removing extra steps.
items.example: We streamlined onboarding from six forms to one.

items.definition: To fail to notice something, or to decide to ignore a small fault.
items.example: It is easy to overlook a typo in your own writing.

translations.bn: উপেক্ষা করা বা খেয়াল না করা

items.definition: A disadvantage of something that is otherwise good.
items.example: The main drawback of the free plan is the storage limit.

items.definition: General agreement among a group of people.
items.example: After an hour we reached a consensus on the budget.

items.definition: The latest time by which something must be finished.
items.example: The deadline for applications is the fifth of March.

items.definition: A clear, useful understanding of how something really works.
items.example: The interviews gave us real insight into why users leave.

items.definition: A difference between two things that should match.
items.example: There is a discrepancy between the invoice and the receipt.

items.definition: An important point of progress in a longer project or journey.
items.example: Finishing the first draft was a real milestone.

items.definition: A small difference in meaning, tone, or feeling.
items.example: Translation often loses the nuance of the original.

items.definition: A problem that delays progress or pushes you backwards.
items.example: Losing the data was a setback, but we recovered in a week.

items.definition: In the end, after a long time or several delays.
items.example: The bus eventually arrived forty minutes late.

items.definition: Used to say something can reasonably be argued, though others may disagree.
items.example: This is arguably the clearest chapter in the book.

items.definition: On purpose, not by accident.
items.example: The form is deliberately short so more people finish it.

items.definition: Approximately; close to a number but not exact.
items.example: The walk takes roughly twenty minutes.

items.definition: To understand something or find the answer after thinking about it.
items.example: It took me a while to figure out how the app saves files.

translations.bn: বুঝে ফেলা বা সমাধান বের করা

items.definition: To continue doing what you were doing.
items.example: Carry on with the exercise while I check the answers.

items.definition: To stop trying, or to stop doing something you used to do.
items.example: Don't give up after one bad practice test.

items.definition: To tell someone about something they may not have noticed.
items.example: She pointed out that the numbers on page two don't add up.

items.definition: To start talking about a subject.
items.example: I'll bring up the budget question in tomorrow's meeting.

items.definition: To find something by chance, or to give a certain impression to others.
items.example: I came across an old photo while cleaning my desk.

items.definition: To decide that something is not possible or not the cause.
items.example: We can rule out a network problem — the logs are clean.

items.definition: To check again later, or to take the next step after something.
items.example: I'll follow up with the supplier on Monday.

items.definition: To stop insisting on something after opposition.
items.example: Neither side would back down, so the meeting ended early.

items.definition: To end well, or to calculate or solve something.
items.example: I was nervous about the move, but it worked out well.

items.definition: To refuse an offer, or to reduce the volume or level of something.
items.example: He turned down the job because of the commute.

items.definition: To stop working, or to separate something into smaller parts.
items.example: Let's break down the project into weekly tasks.

translations.bn: ছোট ভাগে ভাগ করা; বিকল হওয়া

items.definition: To investigate something to learn more about it.
items.example: Support said they would look into the billing error.

items.definition: To reach a situation or place that you did not plan.
items.example: We ended up staying an extra night because of the storm.

items.definition: To prepare or arrange something so it is ready to use.
items.example: It only takes a minute to set up the extension.

items.definition: To delay something until later.
items.example: Don't put off the application until the last day.

items.definition: To use all of something so that none is left.
items.example: We ran out of time before the last question.

items.definition: To have a friendly relationship with someone.
items.example: She gets along with everyone on the team.

items.definition: To reach the same level as others, or to share news with someone after time apart.
items.example: Let's catch up over coffee next week.

translations.bn: পিছিয়ে পড়া অবস্থা পুষিয়ে নেওয়া; খোঁজখবর নেওয়া

items.definition: To deal with a problem successfully, or to organize things.
items.example: I need an hour to sort out my notes before the exam.

items.definition: To choose to believe someone when you are not completely sure what happened.
items.example: I'll give her the benefit of the doubt because she has always been reliable.

translations.bn: সন্দেহ থাকা সত্ত্বেও কাউকে বিশ্বাস করার সুযোগ দেওয়া
translations.zh-CN: 在有疑问时暂且相信某人

items.definition: To stop appreciating something, or to assume it is true without checking.
items.example: We take clean water for granted until it stops running.

translations.bn: মূল্য না দেওয়া বা যাচাই ছাড়াই ধরে নেওয়া

items.definition: To commit even harder to a choice, especially after it is criticized.
items.example: Instead of apologizing, he doubled down on his original claim.

translations.bn: সমালোচনার পরেও নিজের অবস্থানে আরও জোর দেওয়া

items.definition: Said to show you accept someone's reason, even if you don't fully agree.
items.example: "I'd rather review it tomorrow." "Fair enough."

items.definition: Slightly ill.
items.example: I'm a bit under the weather, so I'll join the call from home.

items.definition: Understanding a situation in the same way as someone else.
items.example: Let's talk for five minutes so we're on the same page.

translations.bn: একই বিষয়ে একমত বা সমঝোতায় থাকা

items.definition: Over a long period of time, rather than immediately.
items.example: Studying a little every day pays off in the long run.

items.definition: Completely unexpectedly, with no warning.
items.example: She called me out of the blue after five years.

items.definition: A rough practical guideline that works most of the time.
items.example: As a rule of thumb, keep slides to one idea each.

items.definition: Said when something sounds simple but is hard to actually do.
items.example: "Just wake up at five." That's easier said than done.

items.definition: To warn someone about something in advance.
items.example: Give me a heads-up if the meeting moves.

items.definition: To learn how to do something after some practice.
items.example: The shortcuts feel odd at first, but you'll get the hang of it.

translations.bn: চর্চার পর কৌশলটা রপ্ত করে ফেলা

items.definition: To do more than what is required.
items.example: He went the extra mile and rewrote the guide in plain English.

items.definition: To fail to understand the most important part of what was said.
items.example: You're missing the point — speed isn't the issue, accuracy is.

items.definition: To finally decide between choices.
items.example: Make up your mind before the tickets sell out.

items.definition: Said to show you are not angry after a disagreement or a loss.
items.example: You got the role instead of me — no hard feelings.

translations.bn: মনে কোনো রাগ বা ক্ষোভ নেই

items.definition: To save time or money by skipping steps, usually hurting quality.
items.example: They cut corners on testing and paid for it later.

translations.bn: সহজ পথ ধরে মান নষ্ট করা

items.definition: To force yourself to do something unpleasant that you have been avoiding.
items.example: I finally bit the bullet and rewrote the whole chapter.

translations.bn: কষ্টকর কাজটা সাহস করে করে ফেলা

items.definition: To decide what to do as the situation develops, instead of planning ahead.
items.example: We don't know the weather yet, so let's play it by ear.

items.definition: To make brief contact with someone to share an update.
items.example: Let's touch base on Friday before the client call.

items.definition: To decide something. English uses "make", not "take", with this noun.
items.example: We need to make a decision by the end of the week.

items.definition: To accept that something is your duty or your fault.
items.example: She took responsibility for the delay and apologized.

items.definition: To finish something by the required time.
items.example: We met the deadline with two hours to spare.

items.definition: To formally mention a worry so others can address it.
items.example: Two reviewers raised a concern about the sample size.

items.definition: To decide what something means based on the evidence.
items.example: It is too early to draw a conclusion from one survey.

items.definition: To watch or listen carefully.
items.example: Pay attention to the units in the second question.

items.definition: To remember something while you make a decision.
items.example: Keep in mind that the office closes at six.

items.definition: To include something as a factor when judging or deciding.
items.example: The score takes attendance into account.

items.definition: To finish a negotiation with both sides accepting the same terms.
items.example: The two teams reached an agreement after a long call.

items.definition: A point that is well supported and hard to disagree with.
items.example: That's a strong argument for keeping the current design.
